items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: You know, you’d play in local bands and then Ben and others may have joined Duke’s band, and so I think they were forced to do that.

ctx.x: Before we leave this sound question, what are the actual — I mean you said this great thing just a while ago about the mouthpieces and the reed and you actually answered my question before I asked it. What else actually goes into this sound question. I mean when you say you can identify any number of people from one phrase, what makes that happen? Why does Ben Webster jump off the record as Ben Webster or Coltrane?

Well I just think that during that time period I think there was a real emphasis on kind of finding your own way and finding your own path, and developing your own sound. You have to also realize that these musicians existed before there was — you know jazz education was even an apple in somebody’s eye. I mean they had the opportunity to develop musicianship on the bandstand when they were out playing, probably from a very young age. You know, you’d play in local bands and then Ben and others may have joined…

helping you in the long run to kind of find who you are and discover who you are as a musician? And for me it’s also, it’s not just music that goes into creating the sound, it’s like how you live, what kind of books you read, what kind of movies you watch, what kind of people you hang out with. I mean that all has a big effect on how you play.
